TimelineIndexAccessor::argsort¶

Back to Timeline Index Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

pluss::Series TimelineIndexAccessor::argsort() const

What It Does¶

Returns the integer permutation that would sort the index.

It is the reusable ordering plan. That is the distinction from sort(), which returns the reordered axis directly.

Returns¶

pluss::Series A 1D integer permutation.

Examples¶

auto dup = pluss::timeindex::make({
    "2024-11-01T00:40:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T00:00:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T00:20:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T00:20:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T01:00:00Z",
}, false);

auto out = dup.argsort();
std::cout << pluss::series::print(out) << "\n";

Output¶

Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 2, 3, 0, 4]

Example 2. Reuse the same permutation on the index and any aligned value payload.

auto order = dup.argsort();
auto sorted_idx = dup.take(order);
std::cout << pluss::series::print(order) << "\n";
std::cout << pluss::timeindex::print(sorted_idx) << "\n";
// values.take(order) would follow the same temporal order

Notes¶

  • argsort() is especially useful when you need to sort multiple aligned payloads the same way.
